name: greed
quote: She ate all of our chocolates!
description: Having or desiring for more of something than is considered decent by a particular social group.

variations.name: realized greed
variations.description: If you come to perceive that others are correct in considering your actions greedy, you may experience embarassment or guilt.
examples: So sorry, I didn't know I was only supposed to have one.

variations.name: push your luck
variations.description: Risking the loss of something valuable to get something perceived as even more valuable.
examples: He'd already won a lot, but decided to roll the dice again.

variations.name: hoarding
variations.description: Collecting assets for 'later use' and then not using or sharing them when appropriate.
examples: They have a pantry full of wine, but drank ours instead.

variations.name: stinginess
variations.description: Giving to others things of less value than is socially expected.
examples: All dad gave me for my birthday was a pack of gum.

commentaries.quote: Most often 'greed' is a label applied to others. What the 'greedy' person experiences may be ambition to succeed or fear of not having enough for the future.
Greed can be considered a positive motivation in a free-market economy.

Asset accumulation is considered negative when it exceeds societal expectations about how they're supposed to be distributed. For example, even just having 2 cookies could be considered greedy if everyone was supposed to have only one.

conditions: Having or desiring more of something.
Social judgement that you already have enough or too much of that thing.
